scenario.title: Composite multi-stage intrusion - tabletop simulation
scenario.framework: NIST SP 800-61 Rev.2 incident handling lifecycle / SANS PICERL
boundary_statement: Every stage is represented by real, hash-verifiable evidence that already exists in Week-2 (datasets, OpenObserve alert evidence, verified timelines) and Week-3 (tickets, audit logs).

The datasets come from different public sources and different years. The chain that links the stages is a scenario construct for the tabletop exercise; causal links between stages are NOT observed in the data.
Timeline order is the scenario stage order. Timestamps shown are the original dataset timestamps and are never shifted or invented.
No live SIEM, no live TheHive, no live threat-intelligence feed, no remediation is executed. Containment/eradication/recovery items are proposals that require a recorded analyst decision.

stages.name: Reconnaissance
stages.question_for_analysts: Is the vertical port scan from an authorised scanner, and which hosts/services were exposed?

stages.name: Web-tier attack
stages.question_for_analysts: Did any XSS payload execute in a browser, and is the high-rate HTTP source linked to the scan?

stages.name: Credential attack
stages.question_for_analysts: Did any SSH password guess succeed (Accepted password) for root or another account?

stages.name: Execution
stages.question_for_analysts: Is the dropped executable malicious (hash verdict), and did the reverse-shell connection succeed?

stages.name: Persistence and privilege-sensitive activity
stages.question_for_analysts: Is the Winlogon Shell modification authorised, and were the sudo commands approved administration?

stages.name: Discovery and defense evasion
stages.question_for_analysts: Who cleared the Security log (Event 1102) and was it part of approved maintenance?

stages.name: Lateral movement
stages.question_for_analysts: Which client and account initiated the WinRM command execution on the domain controller?

stages.name: Command and control
stages.question_for_analysts: Are the periodic connections, DNS chunk burst and plink tunnel C2 channels or approved tooling?

stages.name: Collection / exfiltration (hypothesis)
stages.question_for_analysts: Did the mailbox export requests complete, and do the exported .aspx files exist on the server?

ai.summary: Two suspicious Exchange mailbox export requests were detected on win-dc-exch01.attackrange.local, potentially indicating unauthorized data exfiltration.

semantic_warnings: The original AI summary suggests possible unauthorized data exfiltration; no unauthorized access or exfiltration is confirmed.
The AI omitted the key indicator: ASPX export destinations within the Exchange OWA web directory.
The source log reports cmdlet success, but actual export completion and file creation are not independently verified.
The AI incorrectly categorized the original-versus-replay timestamp distinction as an unverified hypothesis.
The AI repeated missing-evidence items under unverified hypotheses instead of separating hypotheses from verification requirements.
The original semantic_warnings array was empty despite these review findings.

prohibited_detail.reason: Exchange receiver hard-codes qa_status=REVIEW_REQUIRED; no proposed response actions permitted
Tier 2 prohibited
Exchange report §11: 'Do not automatically isolate hosts or disable accounts'
Evidence unverified; no filesystem/IIS proof of completion
Tier 2 prohibited

limitations: The export requests were unauthorized.
The ASPX destination paths were intended for web-shell staging.
The requested export operations resulted in actual files on disk.
Any web shell was deployed, accessed, or executed.
Any mailbox data was successfully exfiltrated.
Cmdlet audit log shows the export requests were removed and Search-Mailbox -DeleteContent ran after each export; export file creation on disk is still not shown by any log in the repository.
